classification.method: expected class from the harness (new $LATEST config -> cold; new published version -> restore; reused environment -> warm), checked against REPORT (Init Duration / Restore Duration / neither)

conclusion: Baseline pinned. Cold start is dominated by the weight download (p50 25.0 s of 36.0 s, 79 MiB/s from one environment) and mmap/model load (8.4 s). SnapStart restore p50 3.3 s plus a 0.67 s first request on Graviton3. Warm engine p50 0.62 s on Graviton3, 1.07 s on Graviton2. Run-to-run CV of per-round medians: cold 0.4%, restore 2.6%, warm 5.4% (instrumented arm). Instrumentation overhead within matched CPU parts is below the run-to-run spread on every class. 1,200 invocations, 0 errors, 0 class mismatches, answers bit-identical per CPU part.

conditions.weight_fetch: HEAD + parallel 64 MiB ranged GETs (32 threads) into a memfd (examples/lambda/app/loader.py); llama.cpp mmaps /proc/self/fd/N

correctness.method: complete answer object, same request id and same CPU part as the reference

cost.s3_transfer_note: S3 to Lambda in the same region: no data transfer charge

deployment.az: not exposed to the function; Lambda chooses per environment

hypothesis: None: the pinned reference. Every experiment changes one variable against this deployment and request set.

instrumentation_overhead.method: median(inst) - median(rep) within each CPU part both arms ran on; Lambda REPORT numbers and the in-function engine latency, which both arms emit

model.transform: LoRA merged fp32 (weights/merge_export.py), H512 Hadamard fold (weights/fold_hadamard.py --block 512)
